hyps.why: Edge 0 only reaches the output through edge 4 or the 1->2->3 route, so a conv on it is worth less when edge 4 is cut.
With edge 1 removed, edge 5 is only reachable via the 0->1->2 route, so its upgrade gives less benefit.
When the 1->3 path is removed, the direct conv carries more of the representational load, so adding it helps more.
A strong conv already on edge 5 makes the extra conv on the direct edge redundant, giving diminishing returns.
Edge 4 is fed by node 1, which is dead when edge 0 is none, so the edit has almost no effect.
Edge 2 takes input from node 1, which is disconnected when edge 0 is none, so the edit does nothing.
Node 2 output is useful only via edge 5, so the edge 1 conv gains nothing when edge 5 is cut.
Removing a weak avg_pool costs less than removing a skip or conv, so the edit is less harmful when it replaces avg_pool.
Replacing a strong conv with pooling loses much more accuracy than replacing a weaker op.
Downgrading a conv to a skip on the first edge hurts more than the skip edit does on average, since a skip adds no learned features.
